sections.note: Topic: Language and Literature Career Practicum. This course explores career and educational opportunities for foreign language and literature majors, elaborates the skills gained in the major, and engages students in long-term career planning and preparation. Students research organizations, learn about particular jobs, research graduate school options, and prepare to present their skills to employers.

Language & Minorities in Europe. Credit: 3 or 4 hours. Survey of regional and immigrant minority language use, policies, and planning across Europe. Focus on political and social issues, such as language regimes, education, loss, and maintenance. Two immigrant languages, Turkish and Arabic/Berber, and four indigenous language families: Balto-Slavic with Estonian, Celtic, Romance with Basque, and Slavic with Hungarian. Taught in English. Same as GER 418, ITAL 418, LING 418, PS 418, SLAV 418, SPAN 418, and EURO 418. 3 undergraduate hours. 4 graduate hours.

This course examines historical and scholarly debates about the (post)coloniality of the Central and East European regions. Students will read and analyze new theoretical and empirical studies about the applicability of the colonial and postcolonial paradigms to the region’s past and present.
